question: A 50-year-old woman presents with progressive dysphagia to both solids and liquids from the onset, regurgitation of undigested food (not acid), and nocturnal coughing. A barium swallow shows a 'bird-beak' tapering at the lower oesophagus. What is the most likely diagnosis and its underlying pathophysiological mechanism?

answers.text: Oesophageal carcinoma — mucosal invasion causing progressive luminal narrowing

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Oesophageal carcinoma typically causes solid-only dysphagia initially, progressing to liquids as the lumen narrows. The simultaneous solid-and-liquid dysphagia from the outset, undigested food regurgitation, and bird-beak appearance are characteristic of achalasia, not carcinoma.

answers.text: Achalasia — failure of lower oesophageal sphincter relaxation due to loss of myenteric (Auerbach's) plexus ganglion cells

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Achalasia results from destruction of inhibitory ganglion cells in Auerbach's myenteric plexus, leading to absent peristalsis and failure of LOS relaxation. The bird-beak narrowing at the gastro-oesophageal junction, simultaneous solid+liquid dysphagia, and regurgitation of undigested food are pathognomonic.

answers.text: Peptic stricture — acid-induced fibrous scarring of the lower oesophagus

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Peptic stricture is associated with a long GORD history, causes predominantly solid dysphagia, and shows smooth narrowing but not the characteristic bird-beak appearance. Regurgitation of undigested (not acid-tasting) food argues against an acid-peptic process.

answers.text: Plummer-Vinson syndrome — postcricoid web causing oropharyngeal dysphagia in iron-deficient women

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Plummer-Vinson syndrome causes oropharyngeal (not oesophageal) dysphagia due to a postcricoid web, occurs in iron-deficient middle-aged women, and would not produce a bird-beak appearance at the lower oesophagus.

overallFeedback.feedback: Key distinction: simultaneous solid+liquid dysphagia from the outset = motility disorder (achalasia); solid-first then liquids = mechanical obstruction. Bird-beak narrowing on barium swallow is pathognomonic for achalasia.

Excellent. Achalasia's three cardinal features — simultaneous solid+liquid dysphagia, undigested regurgitation, bird-beak barium appearance — reflect the pathophysiology of absent LOS relaxation due to myenteric plexus ganglion cell loss.
